page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-8 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the E2 family. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical AMD EPYC 7B12 cores with multithreading enabled at 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates a balanced performance profile. The single-core CPU performance measured via stress-ng is strong, placing in the top 25% with a score of 2681.48. Multi-core performance, Geekbench scores, and Passmark CPU metrics generally fall within the average range. Memory bandwidth tests show average throughput, with read-only small block cached speeds at 507.84 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 46.34 GB/sec. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Passmark extended instructions tests represent areas of weaker performance, falling into the bottom 25%.

This instance is designed for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it suitable for database operations, caching layers like Redis, and memory-heavy web serving. It achieves average performance across database operations and Redis SET benchmarks. Given its E2 family classification, it offers a cost-efficient profile for applications requiring high memory density without the premium cost of specialized compute-heavy or storage-heavy hardware classes.
